vBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-2265: fix GitHub GraphQL quota exhaustion — route remaining pollers off gh GraphQL

plan.title: fix: GitHub GraphQL quota exhaustion — top burners and remediation plan
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-4-8

narratives.Problem: GitHub GraphQL quota on the personal eltmon/overdeck token is exhausted. The GitHub App + smee webhook backend is now provisioned (isGitHubAppConfigured() is true, App REST available), but several automated pollers still call gh GraphQL (gh pr view/list, gh issue view/list) UNCONDITIONALLY — they never branch on App config — so they keep burning the GraphQL budget every tick. This routes those remaining pollers onto the App REST path (installation token, separate quota, no GraphQL), replicating the canonical template refreshMergeStateFromGitHub (webhook-handlers.ts:206-257) that already landed in this branch as a5d4148d28.
narratives.Proposal: Add shared App-REST helpers to github-app.ts (foundation bead), then route each remaining gh-GraphQL poller through them with the exact isGitHubAppConfigured() branch the template uses (App REST when configured, existing gh fallback otherwise). The flywheel label fetch drops its GraphQL path entirely (App REST -> gh api REST fallback). The PR/Discussions display tabs get a server-side webhook-aware cache so they refetch from GitHub only on relevant webhooks, not a blind 30s timer. A GraphQL cool-down gate provides defense-in-depth against hammering a depleted budget.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Provisioning the GitHub App / smee relay, or any HMAC / webhook-secret change (ops, already done by the operator).
- Re-implementing refreshMergeStateFromGitHub (already landed as commit a5d4148d28 in this branch).
- Full App-REST reconstruction of the heavy PR/Diff display field set (gh pr view --json files,statusCheckRollup,body,reviewDecision) — deferred to a follow-up issue; the webhook-aware cache already collapses its call frequency and full reconstruction is expert-risk UI work needing dedicated UAT.
- Any frontend change: refetchInterval mechanics, webhook-driven query invalidation, or tab-visibility gating (the cache is server-side; the frontend is untouched).
- auto-merge-eligibility.ts and forge.ts mergeReviewArtifact — already App-aware, verified in scope review.
- Reconciling this branch's local-main vs origin/main divergence (the sync pipeline's job).

autoDecisions.summary: All shared App-REST helpers live in one foundation bead (app-rest-helpers) in github-app.ts.
autoDecisions.rationale: listPullRequestsForHead/getIssueState/listOpenIssuesWithLabels are shared by six consumers; centralizing them mirrors the existing getPullRequestStatePromise and reduces each consumer to a one-branch diff. A wrong return shape would infect all consumers, so the bead is requiresInspection:true.

autoDecisions.summary: The flywheel fallback is gh api REST pagination, not gh issue list GraphQL.
autoDecisions.rationale: The list op has a trivial REST equivalent; removing the GraphQL path entirely guarantees FR-1 even without the App — the sandbox constraint that originally justified gh is satisfied by gh api REST.

autoDecisions.summary: Full App-REST reconstruction of the heavy PR display field set is deferred to a follow-up (NonGoal).
autoDecisions.rationale: It only burns quota while a human has a Command Deck tab open (bounded, self-limiting), the webhook-aware cache collapses its frequency, and reconstructing files/statusCheckRollup/body/reviewDecision across multiple REST endpoints is expert-risk UI work deserving its own issue with UAT.

autoDecisions.summary: The cool-down gate is wired only into the one observed-failing fallback (refreshMergeStateFromGitHub) and exported for later adoption.
autoDecisions.rationale: That gh fallback is the path dashboard.log showed failing repeatedly during exhaustion; over-wiring the gate across every call site would bloat the bead past independent reviewability. Export makes later adoption cheap.

items.title: Add shared App-REST helpers to github-app.ts (PR-by-head, issue-state, open-issue-labels)

expected_outputs: github-app helper tests pass, asserting the owner-qualified head param and REST paths

narrative.Action: In src/lib/github-app.ts, mirror the existing getPullRequestStatePromise (:398) / getPullRequestState Effect wrapper (:691) — both built on the internal githubApi<T>() helper (:257) — to add three exported App-REST helpers, each with a *Promise form and an Effect-wrapped form: (1) listPullRequestsForHead(owner, repo, branch, state:'open'|'closed'|'all') -> Array<{number,state,merged,mergedAt}> via GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls?head={owner}:{branch}&state={state}; (2) getIssueState(owner, repo, number) -> {state:'open'|'closed'} via GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{number}; (3) listOpenIssuesWithLabels(owner, repo) -> Array<{number,labels:string[]}> via paginated GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues?state=open&per_page=100, filtering out entries that are pull requests. Add unit tests mocking githubApi that assert each request path and return shape, including that the pulls head param is OWNER-qualified (owner:branch).

items.title: listPullRequestsForHead returns PRs via GET /pulls?head={owner}:{branch}&state={state} (App REST), and its test asserts the head param is owner-qualified — no GraphQL
getIssueState returns {state} from GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{number} (App REST)
listOpenIssuesWithLabels returns each open issue's number and labels via paginated REST and excludes pull-request entries
importing each helper returns both a Promise form and an Effect-wrapped form, matching the getPullRequestState convention
Route flywheel open-issue-label fetch off gh GraphQL (App REST, gh api REST fallback)

Otherwise fall back to gh api REST pagination (gh api 'repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues?state=open&per_page=100' with page traversal), NOT gh issue list. Preserve the existing try/catch degrade-to-empty posture exactly — the function must never throw when run in a credential-less sandbox.

Serve PR + Discussions tab data from a webhook-aware server cache

expected_outputs: cache tests show a cached hit avoids a GitHub fetch and a webhook bump forces a refetch

narrative.Action: Add a per-issue cache-generation map (new src/dashboard/server/services/pr-tab-cache.ts, or an in-module singleton) that webhook handlers bump. In src/lib/webhook-handlers.ts, have handlePullRequest, handlePullRequestReview, and the issue_comment handler bump the affected issue's generation. In src/dashboard/server/routes/issues.ts, make the /api/issues/:id/pr and /api/issues/:id/discussions handlers cache their response keyed by (issueId, generation): serve the cache and skip the GitHub fetch when the generation is unchanged; refetch and re-cache when it bumps or the cache is cold. Do NOT change the heavy gh pr view field set or the frontend refetchInterval — only gate when GitHub is actually hit.

items.title: GET /api/issues/:id/pr serves the cached response without calling GitHub when the issue's cache generation is unchanged
after a pull_request / pull_request_review / issue_comment webhook bumps the issue's generation, the next /pr fetch emits a fresh GitHub request
GET /api/issues/:id/discussions serves its cache on an unchanged generation and emits a fresh GitHub request after a webhook bump
a cold cache (no prior fetch) still produces a full response on the first request
Add a GraphQL rate-limit cool-down gate (defense-in-depth)

expected_outputs: cool-down tests pass using fake timers — true within 60s, false after

narrative.Action: Create src/lib/github-graphql-cooldown.ts exporting noteGraphQLRateLimit(err: unknown) — records a cool-down start when the error message matches a GraphQL-quota-exceeded pattern (e.g. /rate limit already exceeded/i or /API rate limit/i) — and isInGraphQLCooldown(): boolean — true for COOLDOWN_MS (~60000) after the last note. Wire it into refreshMergeStateFromGitHub's gh fallback (src/lib/webhook-handlers.ts:239): skip the doomed gh pr view GraphQL call and note the rate-limit when isInGraphQLCooldown() is true / on a caught rate-limit error. The timing test MUST use vi.useFakeTimers() + vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync() — no real setTimeout waits.

items.title: after noteGraphQLRateLimit() with a quota-exceeded error, isInGraphQLCooldown() returns true within ~60s and false thereafter (verified with fake timers)
while isInGraphQLCooldown() is true, refreshMergeStateFromGitHub's gh fallback emits no gh GraphQL call and returns without hitting GitHub
after noteGraphQLRateLimit() with an unrelated (non-rate-limit) error, isInGraphQLCooldown() returns false
